verdict: FAIL-AT-G4-AS-PLANNED (route PASS; clock OCV FAIL; seam hold FAIL; ft repeaters/budget WARN)
reasons: [2026-10-24 12:30] [TRIAL-HBM visual review, owner order 08:05] ## Visual review (owner order 08:05: rendered, looked at, findings)  Renders: - `render/floorplan.png`: partitions by role, hard cores, keep-outs, lane bundles, H-tree; - `render/congestion.png` (derate 0.5) and `render/congestion_adj097.png` (M8/M9 only); - `render/hops.png`: hops > 700 um; - `clock/htree_built.png`, `clock/tap_latency_heatmap.png`; - the IR maps in `ir/`.  What looks wrong: 1. **Data flow from the PHY.**    - The 9.4 kbit/row PHY <-> hub traffic leaves PHY_N at its S-face corners. It runs W/E through the empty mcb corners on M4/M8 (`congestion_adj097`: M8 block at y 16.3-17.3 mm, x 5.5-8.5).    - It then turns down the narrow spt columns (1.8 mm wide) for about 6 mm to the su row and the hub.    - In the M8/M9-only case those columns sit at 0.7-0.86 of raw M9.    - It is the longest wire class on the die (SM_HBM 25 cycles in the price) and is routed through the partitions built to hold it, so it is by design. It has no spare capacity for ECO or for widening the PHY interface. 2. **The central window.** The old die failed in one central window. B2r2 still concentrates its traffic at the die centre bottom:    - `root`'s bottom-left corner and the hc-ring bottom bank row b000..b003 / b000'..b003' form a continuous M8 band across the seam at y 6.3 mm;    - a hot M8/M9 spot sits at (12.5, 6.25) mm.     This is the hc ring plus seam traffic. It is the first window to saturate if partition logic needs more M8, and it is the hold-and-skew-critical seam too (the trunk root is there). 3. **Long wires.**    - `hops.png` shows the hop-length distribution is bimodal: about 2-um abutted hops plus a huge 700-960 um population everywhere in the ft corridors (spt, vsN, spu, su rows, b-slices).    - Diagonal-looking long hops inside the hub and b103 (L19_2) are the per-bit spread of wide windows. The station site is shared by all bits, so the edge bits of a 1-2 mm window add up to ~100 um.    - Fix: per-bit station sites (Codex 6c04a26209 added audited per-bit FT sites) or narrower windows. 4. **Seams.**    - The hub's west face toward b112/b113 and io is M9-hot (0.85).    - The NW_b112 | NW_hub pair is also the worst clock seam (it diverges at the root). One partition pair is therefore both route- and clock-critical. 5. **Clock tree shape.**    - A uniform leaf grid ignores tap density: leaves are wasted on the SMs and the mc corners, and the hub / band gets 1.3-mm local nets.    - The trunk runs along the seam column, so the seam pairs share the trunk. But the trunk splits mid-row, so vertical neighbours (su | hub, sm | su) diverge high in the tree. That is where OCV hurts. 6. **Empty corners.** mca/mcb (2 x 2 x 8.7 mm2) carry only clock leaves and the PHY escape. That is wasted area, as the spec already notes.
